edits.old: Keeping the full working set in memory is a performance objective, not a correctness prerequisite. MongoDB's diagnostics FAQ says the working set need not fit in RAM, while its performance guidance allows faster SSDs to complement less RAM when price-performance and workload SLAs justify that trade-off. (high confidence)
edits.new: The working set does not have to fit in RAM: MongoDB's diagnostics FAQ answers 'No' and explains that WiredTiger evicts pages from the cache when it lacks space. MongoDB's production notes say that SSDs or more RAM may be more effective at increasing I/O throughput, and its hardware best-practices guidance says SSDs suit read-heavy applications whose working set no longer fits in memory. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/diagnostics.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/production-notes.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/performance-best-practices-hardware-and-os-configuration

evidence.quote: If the cache does not have enough space to load additional data, WiredTiger evicts pages from the cache to free up space.
Using SSDs or increasing RAM may be more effective in increasing I/O throughput.
SSDs should also be used for read heavy applications if the working set no longer fits in memory.

edits.rationale: The FAQ answers No to whether the working set must fit RAM. The production notes and MongoDB's hardware best-practices blog support SSDs as an alternative or complement to RAM for I/O throughput. No MongoDB source found explicitly ties this to 'workload SLAs' or says SSDs 'complement less RAM', so that framing is dropped.
